sections.heading: Passing, night driving and age-related driving
sections.markdown:
# Passing, night driving and age-related driving

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
The guide permits passing to the right where at least two lanes carry traffic in the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Do not leave the roadway and use the shoulder to pass, even if the shoulder is paved. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
A driver being passed on the right might not see the passing vehicle and could move into its lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
On a multilane roadway, the far-left lane is intended for passing slower traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not approach closely behind a vehicle in preparation for passing because it blocks the forward view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Wait at a safe distance until the road ahead can be seen far enough to judge a pass safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
The guide advises against attempting a pass when an opposing vehicle is visible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A02
Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots to make sure another vehicle is not already overtaking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A02
Signal before moving out to pass and check for vehicles entering from side roads or driveways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A02
Keep watching ahead and avoid drifting toward the vehicle being passed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A02
Before returning to the lane, wait until the front of the passed vehicle can be seen in the rear-view mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A02
Signal again before returning to the original lane after a pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
When another vehicle is passing, make the maneuver easier by reducing speed slightly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane road, a driver being passed should move right as far as can be done safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
Before reversing, check behind the vehicle and look directly through the rear window rather than depending only on mirrors. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
Reverse slowly and remain ready to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
Walking around the vehicle before backing can reveal a child, pet or object in the path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A03
The first rain can make pavement especially slick because water mixes with oil and grease that have not washed away. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A03
On wet pavement, the guide calls for slower travel, extra caution and twice the normal following space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A03
Slow, careful travel, particularly through curves, helps prevent a skid on a wet road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A03
If the car skids, remain calm, ease off the accelerator and steer carefully toward the intended path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A03
The guide advises avoiding brake use during its described wet-road skid recovery. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A03
Hydroplaning occurs when the tires ride over a layer of water rather than remain in contact with pavement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A03
Loss of tire contact during hydroplaning reduces the ability to steer, accelerate or brake effectively. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A03
To regain contact when hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator while looking and steering toward the intended path; avoid braking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A03
Slower wet-road speeds, recommended tire inflation and good tread help reduce hydroplaning risk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
Sloshing tire noise on a wet road is a reason to reduce speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
Never turn the ignition into its steering-lock setting while the vehicle is moving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A04
At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the distance illuminated ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A04
A dirty windshield increases headlight glare and makes road users and signs harder to see. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A04
For night driving, the guide recommends adding at least one second of following space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A04
On an unfamiliar road at night, the guide recommends adding at least two seconds of following space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A04
The guide requires headlights, rather than parking lamps alone, from sunset until sunrise. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A04
Use low beams within five hundred feet of an approaching vehicle or two hundred feet behind another vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A04
The guide requires headlights when precipitation or airborne moisture makes windshield-wiper use necessary. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A04
Headlights are also required when weather prevents the vehicle from being clearly seen at five hundred feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A04
If an approaching driver will not dim bright headlights, slow and use the roadway’s right edge as a guide. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A04
Switch fog lights off when visibility improves; the guide reserves rear fog lamps for seriously reduced visibility. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0080]
